newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriot Denktash says talks will smooth atmosphere.
newsitem.headline: Cypriot Denktash says talks will smooth atmosphere.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash said on Wednesday he hoped to dispel some of the tension in his relationship with Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides at talks in Nicosia next week.
"I always believed that just meeting and talking, having a coffee together, would be helpful in smoothing the atmosphere around us," Denktash told Reuters in a written statement.
He said the pair would meet in the residence of U.N. representative Gustave Feissel on Monday in a follow-up to talks between the two rivals in the United States earlier this month.
But Denktash said that a bid to give European Union membership to the Greek Cypriot-dominated government in the south of the island could jeopardise future talks.

He said a Greek Cypriot application for EU membership should "be treated for what it is, namely an application by the Greek Cypriot side only, and be put aside so that the August talks are not prejudiced".
The leaders are scheduled to meet again in Switzerland in mid-August for higher-level talks.

Denktash, who heads a breakaway state recognised only by Turkey, said Monday's meeting would involve discussion of humanitarian issues with Clerides, the leader of a Greek Cypriot administration regarded abroad as the Mediterranean island's only government.

The pair met in New York state earlier this month under the auspices of the United Nations for the first time in three years in an attempt to revive stalled negotiations on Cypriot reunification as a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation.
Turkey invaded the northern third of Cyprus on July 20, 1974 after a Greek Cypriot coup backed by the military then ruling Greece.
Previous inter-communal talks have produced little.
Turkish Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit has called for partial integration of north Cyprus with Turkey in retaliation for the EU's planned membership talks with the Greek Cypriots.
